title: Microservices Security Fundamentals
description: Learn the fundamentals of securing microservices architectures.

data.text: Microservices security is more complex than monolith security because the attack surface is larger. Amazon, Google, and Stripe all treat security as a first-class concern, implementing defense in depth across every layer of their microservices.

Security in microservices follows the same principles as any system but with additional complexity. Defense in depth means securing every layer. Zero trust means never trusting any service by default, even internal ones.

data.title: Microservices Security Layers
items: Network: Firewalls, VPNs, mTLS, network policies
API Gateway: Authentication, rate limiting, WAF
Service: Authorization, input validation, output encoding
Data: Encryption at rest and in transit, secrets management
Infrastructure: Container security, image scanning, least privilege

data.title: Zero Trust
data.text: Zero trust means never trust any service by default, even if it is internal. Always authenticate and authorize every request. This is critical because compromised internal services can access sensitive data.

data.title: Example: Security Checklist
A security checklist for microservices.

# Microservices Security Checklist

## Network Layer
- [ ] Use TLS for all internal communication
- [ ] Implement mTLS between services
- [ ] Restrict network access with firewall rules
- [ ] Use Kubernetes NetworkPolicies

## API Layer
- [ ] Authenticate all requests at the gateway
- [ ] Implement rate limiting and WAF
- [ ] Validate all input data
- [ ] Use OAuth2/OIDC for authentication

## Service Layer
- [ ] Authorize every request
- [ ] Never trust client input
- [ ] Sanitize outputs to prevent injection
- [ ] Log security events

## Data Layer
- [ ] Encrypt sensitive data at rest
- [ ] Use secrets management (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager)
- [ ] Rotate credentials regularly
- [ ] Audit data access

items.question: Is microservices security harder than monolith security?
items.answer: Yes, because the attack surface is larger and there are more moving parts. However, security boundaries are clearer, which can make auditing easier.

items.question: What is the OWASP Top 10 for microservices?
items.answer: OWASP Top 10 API Security Risks covers microservices-specific vulnerabilities: broken authentication, excessive data exposure, lack of resources, mass assignment, and more.

items.question: How do I handle security in CI/CD?
items.answer: Use SAST (static analysis), DAST (dynamic testing), and container scanning in your pipeline. Fail builds on critical vulnerabilities.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Microservices have a larger attack surface than monoliths
Defense in depth secures every layer
Zero trust means never trusting internal services by default
Security must be built into the development lifecycle
data.takeaway: Security is everyone's responsibility; implement defense in depth across all microservices layers.
